why.perfect: Perfect cadence: the dominant resolves to the tonic, the strongest rest.
why.deceptive: Deceptive cadence: the tonic is expected, the relative comes. A soft surprise.
why.plagalBack: Back to the subdominant: the tension falls without concluding.
why.toDominant: To the dominant: tension rises and calls for the tonic.
why.plagal: Plagal cadence (IV-I): the "amen", a softer rest than V-I.
why.home: Back to the tonic: you land.
why.preDominant: Prepares the dominant (ii-V): the most natural way into V.
why.subdominant: Subdominant: away from home without tension.
why.dominant: Dominant: the tension that wants to go back to the tonic.
why.relative: Relative: the same notes, the opposite colour (major and minor).
why.secondaryDominant: Secondary dominant of {to}: a chord outside the scale pushing towards {to}.
why.borrowedIv: iv borrowed from minor: a touch of melancholy in a major key.
why.borrowed: Chord borrowed from the minor mode: darker, common in pop and rock.
why.dorianIV: Major IV (Dorian colour): brightens a minor song, very soul.
why.picardy: Picardy third: ending a minor song in major, a bright effect.
why.suspension: Suspension: delays the third, then resolves to {to}.
why.tritoneSub: Tritone substitution: V7 replaced by the chord a tritone away, the bass falls a semitone to {to}.
why.neapolitan: Neapolitan chord: major bII, dramatic, often before {to}.
why.passingDim: Passing diminished: links two chords by a semitone.
why.backdoor: Backdoor cadence: bVII7 to {to}, a more soulful resolution than V7.
why.extend: The same chord, richer (9th): more colour, same function.
why.soulNinth: Ninth chord: the signature of soul keys.
why.funkSharp9: 7#9: the funk chord (Hendrix, James Brown), tense and raw.
why.reggaeSkank: Reggae changes: play it as a skank, short chords on beats 2 and 4.
why.fanfareCadence: Brass band cadence: a plain V7 then the tonic, with the horns.
why.epicCadence: Epic cadence bVI-bVII-I: the rise of film music.
why.sus2Pad: Sus2: open and airy, ideal for a string pad.

var.swap: One chord swapped for another of the same function: same role, another colour
var.borrowIv: The IV turned minor (borrowed from the minor mode): more wistful
var.dominant: A dominant 7 before the return: tension that calls what comes next
var.sevenths: All sevenths: richer, more jazz or soul

why.axis: The most used progression in pop: steady, bright, it goes round forever
why.axisMinorStart: The same starting on vi: more moving, very EDM
why.royal: J-pop's "royal road": it climbs, then falls on the relative
why.canon: Pachelbel's canon: a falling bass, eight chords
why.twoFiveOne: Jazz's ii-V-I: the most natural cadence to the tonic
why.turnaround: The jazz turnaround: an endless loop back to the tonic
why.mixo: The bVII borrowed from mixolydian: rock, without the V's tension
why.borrowedIv: The borrowed iv at the end: the soulful, wistful touch
why.plagalRock: Simple and solid: rock, reggae, folk
why.sadPop: Starting on IV: pop that hangs between joy and regret
why.neoSoul: A descent in sevenths: neo-soul, R&B
why.epic: The epic minor loop: soundtracks, EDM, dark pop
why.andalusian: The Andalusian cadence: the bass falls to V, flamenco and rock
why.aeolianLoop: Natural minor back and forth: wistful rock and electronic
why.minorCadence: The classic minor cadence, the major V bringing it home
why.harmonicDrama: Harmonic minor's major V: dramatic, orchestral
why.circle: The circle of fifths in minor: each chord calls the next
why.dorian: Dorian's major IV: soul and funk groove in minor
why.phrygian: The phrygian bII: dark and tense, very trap and drill
why.darkPop: A minor v instead of V: dark pop and hip-hop, never resolved
why.lament: A short descent that lingers: hip-hop, dreamy rock
why.lofi: Sevenths in a cycle: lo-fi, jazzy hip-hop
